MonitoringProgramDescription:
Area burned is the acres of wildfire inside the Basin each year. It is the observed record that the modeled measures, burn probability and likely fire severity, are checked against.

For most of the last century the Basin saw few large fires, a result of fire suppression rather than of a forest that does not burn. The 2007 Angora Fire burned about 3,100 acres and 254 homes near South Lake Tahoe. The 2021 Caldor Fire burned about 9,900 acres inside the Basin, the largest fire in the record here, before firefighters stopped it in treated forest near Meyers.
MonitoringApproach:
Fire perimeters come from CAL FIRE's statewide fire history, which maps fires on the California side of the Basin; Nevada fires and many small fires are not in it. Each perimeter is clipped to the TRPA boundary and measured in California Albers, so a fire that started outside the Basin counts only the acres that burned inside it.

The Tahoe Fire and Fuels Team fire history, 1988 to 2025, covers both states and will replace this record once it is published.
